title: The Ground
summary: Oisin returns to Ireland three hundred years late and finds his father's hall gone to thorn and moss. A single-character piece: the payoff to Niamh's warning, ending on the line that dooms him.

scenes.visual: Wide shot. The warrior small among the collapsed moss-covered stones of a ring-fort under heavy flat overcast, bare black thorn trees around him. Static camera, low horizon.

dialogue.line: I told her it would be stones and dust. I was right. Being right is worth nothing at all.

scenes.visual: Three-quarter shot from the waist up, reverse angle. The warrior looking at a gap in the fallen wall, grey light on his face. Static camera.

dialogue.line: This was the hall. That was the door my father carried me through when I was small.

scenes.visual: Medium shot from the waist up, seen from the side, bare thorn branches crossing the frame behind him. Static camera.

dialogue.line: The thorn trees have had three hundred years to grow where the fire was. Nobody stopped them.

scenes.visual: Medium shot over the shoulder. The warrior facing the dark opening of the ruin, his back three-quarters to camera. Static camera.

dialogue.line: I keep waiting for someone to come out of the dark and not know my face.

scenes.visual: Close-up. The warrior's face fills much of the frame, the ruin a grey blur behind him, drizzle in the air. He speaks slowly. Static camera.

dialogue.line: I have been sitting on this horse for an hour because I know what happens when I get down. And I am going to get down anyway.

scenes.visual: Wide shot, the warrior small and alone among the stones, the flat grey sky enormous above him. Static camera.

dialogue.line: But there is nobody left to lift me down. So I will have to do it myself.
